questions.question: Explain how the balloon rocket shows the way a real rocket moves.
questions.expected_answer: When you let go of the balloon, air rushes out of the back and the balloon is pushed forwards. A real rocket works in the same way: it pushes hot exhaust gas out of its back end, so the rocket is pushed the other way, up into space.

questions.question: Name four parts of a rocket and say what each one does.
questions.expected_answer: Any four: the nose cone at the top cuts through the air and protects the payload; the payload is what the rocket carries, like a satellite or astronauts; the body holds the fuel tanks; the engine burns the fuel to make hot gas; the nozzle lets the hot gas shoot out the back; the fins keep the rocket flying straight.

questions.question: Describe a rocket as a system with an input, process and output.
questions.expected_answer: The input is the fuel. The process is burning the fuel with oxygen in the engine to make hot gas and pushing that gas out of the nozzle. The output is movement, as the rocket is pushed up into space.
